original_record.question:
Emily has two identical cards in the shape of equilateral triangles. She places them both onto a sheet of paper so that they touch or overlap and draws around the shape she creates. Which one of the following is it impossible for her to draw?
<image1>
original_record.solution: ![](https://cdn.mathpix.com/cropped/2023_12_27_9a6d299634cd335ebb53g-1.jpg?height=135&width=1630&top_left_y=1069&top_left_x=321)  The dotted lines on the diagrams which complete equilateral triangles show that she can create shapes A, B, C and D. Therefore it is shape E that is impossible for her to draw.

answer_verification.reason: A rectangle corner has90degrees. It cannot lie in the edge interior of a contained equilateral triangle, since the triangle locally occupies180degrees there. Thus each rectangle corner must coincide with triangle vertices; one60degree triangle wedge cannot cover90degrees, so both triangles must contribute a vertex at each of4 corners. This requires8triangle vertices, but two triangles have6. Hence E is impossible. A-D have explicit pairs of equilateral triangles in their displayed constructions.
